article_blocks.text: Strain Type: 70% Indica / 30% Sativa
Genetics: Great White Shark × South Indian × Super Skunk
Breeder: Green House Seed Company
THC Content: 17.69%
CBD Content: 0.21%
Terpene Profile: myrcene , pinene , beta-caryophyllene
Primary Flavors: Sweet Skunk, earth, lime, grape, wood
Flowering Time (Indoor): 8 weeks
Outdoor Harvest Time: End of September
Indoor Yield: Up to 800 g/m²
Outdoor Yield: Up to 1,200 g per plant
Grow Difficulty: Intermediate

The Doctor comes from the heavy-production, resin-focused side of Green House Seed Company’s breeding history. Rather than chasing tropical stimulation or long-flowering Haze traits, the Amsterdam breeder combined Great White Shark, South Indian, and Super Skunk to produce marijuana with a compact frame, exceptionally dense flowers, substantial yields, and an effect that moves rapidly toward physical relaxation. Green House describes the high as fast acting, strong, and close to narcotic in intensity, while its current company history places The Doctor alongside Great White Shark as one of its popular indica-oriented cannabis strains with exceptionally hard buds and high production.

The sensory profile is more complex than the plant’s heavy indica reputation might suggest. Skunk and sweet earth establish the base, but cured flower can also reveal lime, fruit, grape, woody spice, and a hash-like finish. At approximately 17.69% THC in Green House’s published specification, the strain does not depend on modern 25–30% laboratory numbers to make its presence felt. Dense resin production, a rapid onset, and a strongly body-centered experience give the cultivar a distinctly old-school personality that fits evening use far better than a demanding daytime schedule.
Genetics and Lineage

The direct lineage is Great White Shark × South Indian × Super Skunk. Great White Shark itself belongs to Green House’s influential “ White family ,” a collection of shorter, bushier cultivars selected for strong flower and resin production. Green House currently describes Great White Shark and The Doctor together as particularly popular among indica enthusiasts and emphasizes the rock-hard structure of their flowers.

Super Skunk contributes a familiar combination of vigorous growth, heavy floral development, penetrating odor, and indica-influenced physical effects. The South Indian component adds another resin-focused branch to the pedigree and connects the strain to the tropical and hash-producing genetics that appear repeatedly in older Green House breeding. Taken together, the family tree favors practical cultivation characteristics: relatively rapid flowering, dense buds, manageable stature, and enough hybrid vigor to support very large harvests.

The result is more nuanced than simply calling it “Skunk with extra indica.” Great White Shark adds a broad resin-heavy foundation, Super Skunk reinforces yield and pungency, and the South Indian material deepens the earthy, spicy, hash-like side of the finished flower. Green House’s own specification classifies the cultivar as 70% indica and 30% sativa, a ratio that makes sense both from plant architecture and from the way the high develops.
Effects and Experience

The Doctor is unusual in how quickly the physical component makes itself known. Green House characterizes the effect as arriving almost immediately and developing into a strong stone that borders on narcotic. Rather than beginning with an extended energetic or creative phase, the experience can move rapidly toward slowed movement, heavier limbs, and a quieter mental state.

There is still a cerebral dimension, especially at smaller amounts. Mood may loosen, conversation can become more amusing, and sensory experiences such as music or food may feel richer. That window can narrow as the dose increases, however. The body becomes progressively heavier, concentration may decline, and the cultivar’s indica side can dominate the session. For many consumers, that makes it far more appropriate for evenings, movies, relaxed social settings, or the end of the day than for work requiring sustained attention.

The breeder-listed THC content of 17.69% should also be interpreted in historical context. Cannabis does not need to test above 25% to feel strong, particularly when dose, tolerance, cannabinoid balance, and individual sensitivity differ so widely. Excessive consumption can still cause dizziness, dry mouth, impaired short-term memory, anxiety, slowed reaction time, or pronounced sleepiness. A calming subjective experience does not eliminate impairment.
Medical Benefits

Green House historically promoted The Doctor for pain and insomnia, which explains both the name and part of the strain’s long-standing reputation. Those descriptions are useful for understanding how the breeder positioned the cultivar, but they should not be mistaken for clinical evidence that The Doctor itself treats either condition. No controlled trials have established strain-specific medical efficacy.

Cannabis research more generally provides some context. Evidence supports potential benefit from certain cannabis or cannabinoid preparations for some forms of chronic pain, while sleep research has produced mixed results depending on the population, cannabinoid formulation, and underlying condition. Those findings cannot automatically be transferred to a specific high-THC flower cultivar because marijuana chemistry varies substantially between crops and individual plants.

The same sedating qualities that some consumers seek may also create problems. THC can produce dizziness, cognitive impairment, sleepiness, altered judgment, anxiety, and coordination difficulties, and cannabinoids can interact with some medications. Medical cannabis patients should therefore rely on current laboratory testing, careful dosing, and appropriate professional guidance rather than assuming the strain’s historical reputation guarantees a particular outcome.
Flavor Profile and Aroma

The aroma begins with unmistakable Skunk. Sweet earth, damp herbal notes, and a pungent cannabis musk form the foundation, but properly cured flower can open into brighter territory as well. Lime and sweet fruit cut through the heavier base, while grape-like tones occasionally appear behind the citrus. The overall bouquet feels far more traditional than contemporary dessert cannabis: pungent first, sweet second.

The flavor develops toward wood and spice on the exhale. Earthy Skunk and citrus can dominate the opening, followed by a drier, more resinous finish reminiscent of hash or incense. The South Indian influence is easiest to imagine in these deeper notes, while Super Skunk helps explain the persistent musk that remains after the brighter fruit has faded.

Myrcene, pinene, and beta-caryophyllene are commonly associated with modern profiles of the cultivar, fitting the earthy, pine-like, herbal, and spicy sensory range. Because Green House does not currently publish a batch-specific terpene percentage panel for every crop, exact concentrations should not be treated as genetically fixed. Storage matters too: warm temperatures and excessive air exposure can quickly weaken lime and fruit aromatics, leaving older flower tasting primarily earthy and woody.
Growing Information

The Doctor was bred with commercial-scale flower production clearly in mind. Green House lists an indoor flowering period of eight weeks and states that an additional week can produce more resin and a sweeter final flavor. Indoor yield can reach approximately 800 grams per square meter in favorable conditions. The cultivar works particularly well with Sea of Green and Screen of Green systems because of its medium stature, dense canopy, and ability to carry numerous heavy flowers.

Bud weight is one of the main horticultural concerns. Green House specifically notes that outdoor plants require support, and the same principle applies indoors when exceptionally large flowers develop. Staking, netting, or trellising can prevent loaded branches from bending or splitting late in bloom. The plant itself remains relatively dense rather than excessively tall, making canopy thinning and good internal airflow particularly important once flowers begin swelling.

Outdoors, harvest falls around the end of September in the Northern Hemisphere. Under ideal conditions Green House lists production as high as approximately 1,200 grams per plant, though that figure should be understood as breeder potential rather than an average guarantee. Plant size, root volume, sunlight, climate, nutrition, phenotype, and training all dramatically affect final production.

Dense flowers create a second challenge: trapped humidity. Reliable air circulation indoors and good branch spacing outdoors become increasingly important as harvest approaches. High-yielding cannabis can look healthy externally while moisture accumulates deep inside compact flowers, so late-stage inspection is worthwhile. Post-harvest handling deserves similar care. Giving the plant the optional additional week suggested by Green House may increase resin and sweetness, but those gains can be lost quickly through an overheated or excessively fast dry.
FAQ
What strain is The Doctor?
The Doctor is an indica-dominant hybrid bred by Green House Seed Company from Great White Shark × South Indian × Super Skunk. Green House classifies it as approximately 70% indica and 30% sativa.
How strong is The Doctor strain?

Green House’s published specification lists approximately 17.69% THC, 0.21% CBD, and 0.06% CBN. Actual cannabinoid concentrations can vary according to phenotype, cultivation conditions, harvest timing, and laboratory methodology.
What does The Doctor taste like?

The flavor combines sweet Skunk and earth with lime, fruit, wood, grape-like sweetness, spice, and a resinous hash-style finish. Proper curing can bring more sweetness forward, while poorly stored flower tends to emphasize the heavier earthy and woody side.
How long does The Doctor take to flower?

Green House lists approximately eight weeks indoors and notes that keeping the plants for an additional week can improve resin production and sweetness. Outdoors, the cultivar is typically ready around the end of September in the Northern Hemisphere.
How much does The Doctor yield?

Breeder specifications list indoor production of up to approximately 800 g/m² and outdoor yields reaching as much as 1,200 grams per plant in optimized conditions. Green House also notes that mature outdoor plants may require structural support because of their heavy flowers.
Final Thoughts on The Doctor

The Doctor reflects the production-driven side of classic Green House Seed Company breeding. Great White Shark, South Indian, and Super Skunk were combined to create a cultivar that could finish quickly, remain reasonably compact, produce exceptionally dense flowers, and deliver an unmistakably heavy indica-oriented experience. Green House still identifies it as one of its popular choices for indica enthusiasts and specifically praises the strain’s high yields and rock-hard buds.

Flavor gives the flower more character than its utilitarian grow traits might suggest. Sweet Skunk and earth dominate the foundation, but lime, fruit, grape, wood, spice, and hash-like resin create enough movement to prevent the smoke from feeling one-dimensional. The effect behaves similarly: some initial mental ease is possible, but physical relaxation quickly takes control and can become strongly sedating at larger doses.

For growers, the combination of an eight-week flowering period, suitability for SOG and ScrOG, indoor yields approaching 800 g/m², and outdoor breeder potential reaching 1,200 g per plant explains why the cultivar developed such a durable reputation. Heavy branches do need support, and the dense flowers demand sensible humidity management, but those are predictable challenges rather than unusual weaknesses.

The Doctor is ultimately a classic high-yielding Green House indica hybrid rather than a modern boutique novelty. Its lineage is well documented, its cultivation characteristics are unusually clear, and its identity has remained consistent: Great White Shark × South Indian × Super Skunk, fast flowering, enormous production potential, pungent old-school flavor, and a body-heavy high that lives up to the strain’s long association with deep relaxation.
